notes: The assertions discriminate well on substance: the run found all four planted changes plus the failing unit test, and the tickets.jsonl artifact independently confirms the CLI was actually driven. Two gaps worth closing. First, check_run.py reports transcript_cli_runs: 5 because the executor abbreviated 'python3 -m ticketdesk.cli' as 'T'; the mechanical check undercounts and the grader has to fall back to reading, so the script should accept an alias definition or the eval should require the literal command in the transcript. Second, the planned case list had 55 cases (incl. X1-X3, X7, X8: missing title arg, unknown option, --log pointing at a directory, --log after subcommand) but the report has 39 and the 'Missing / untested' section does not mention the dropped ones; no assertion checks that every planned case is either in the table or declared untested, so a silent plan-to-report shrink goes uncaught. The prose-lint assertion is the only failure and it is doing real work: 43 findings, mostly semicolons, is the old skill's writing style rather than a test-quality issue, which is exactly what the new skill is meant to fix.
